subject: RFI: Real-world mixed-load benchmarking and scaling behavior
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: perf-team@globex.com
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: mixed real-world load benchmark + scaling behavior

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking this RFI. Globex is preparing a purchase evaluation for a conversational inference platform and we need detailed answers on how Redwood performs under mixed real-world loads (short chat, long-context generation, embedding lookups, and batched reranking). Specifically we're looking for:

- Test methodology you use to simulate combined traffic (ratios, seed prompts).
- Tail-latency measurement approach and sample sizes.
- How throughput scales with added GPU pools and what graceful-degradation modes exist when saturation occurs.
- Kernel selection and quantization impacts for mixed sequences.

Can you share a proposed benchmarking plan, expected metrics for a reference workload (see attached brief), and any artifacts (scripts, config) you can provide to reproduce results?

We'd like an initial reply by EOD Tuesday (17th).

Best,
Priya
Perf Lead, Globex

Attachment: globex_reference_workload_v1.xlsx (attached by Globex)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: mixed real-world load benchmark + scaling behavior

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear ask and the reference workload. We're happy to collaborate. High level plan attached (redwood_mixed_load_plan_v1.pdf). Key notes up front:

- We propose a 3-phase benchmark: baseline characterization (single-model, single-node), mixed-load sweep (ratios: 60% short chat, 25% embeddings + 10% long-gen + 5% rerank), and saturation/flighting tests (step increases in QPS + sudden bursts).
- Tail-latency: 99th and 99.9th percentiles measured with 1M sample windows where possible; reporting windows of 5m/1h.
- Scaling: we will run horizontal scale tests adding identical GPU pools and measure effective QPS per-node and end-to-end token throughput considering batching and KV cache hit rates.
- Degradation modes: model-fallback (smaller quantized variant), regional fallback, and token-throttling with circuit-breaker. We'll document SLO impact for each mode.

Deliverables: proposed workload config (we'll share stresser scripts), kernel-selection matrix for your target models, and a short reproducibility guide. See attached.

Can Karthik and Marcus confirm the kernel matrix and the reproducibility notes? Vanessa — can you include the expected run-time estimate and cost outline?

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_mixed_load_plan_v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: mixed real-world load benchmark + scaling behavior

Folks — quick technical follow-up with specifics we'll include in the final artifact. Highlights: 

- Kernel selection: we build a per-model matrix that maps architecture, sequence buckets, and hardware (A100, H100, L4) to preferred kernels. We'll attach CSV (kernel-selection-matrix.csv). This drives the runtime's choice during mixed loads.
- Quantization: for mixed sequences, we recommend 4-bit quantization for long-context gen models where permissable; short-chat models benefit less from aggressive quantization. We will report delta in latency and quality for int8 and q4h.
- Batching strategy: continuous batching with dynamic batch caps per request type (short vs long). For mixed workloads, we simulate realistic interleaving using a Poisson arrival process with configurable correlation to mimic bursty chat.
- Measurement: use synchronized request ids and a local time sync across runners (NTP + drift checks). We'll provide the runner harness and a reproducible Docker image.

I'll attach the kernel matrix and will include a small sample harness snippet in the shared Drive.

-Karthik
Director, Inference Engineering

Attachments: kernel-selection-matrix.csv

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: perf-team@globex.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: mixed real-world load benchmark + scaling behavior

Thanks — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifications from Globex QA:

1) For the saturation tests, can you define the controlled failure scenarios (e.g., node drop, inter-region latency spike) and how you'll measure failover time?
2) For quantization trade-offs, can you provide sample prompts/labels used to compute quality delta and the acceptance thresholds you'd recommend?
3) We'll want the raw logs (anonymized request ids) and the post-processed metrics (CSV) for our audit. Is that feasible?

Would like to align on these before we accept the run estimate.

Best,
Priya

On a practical note: can you also confirm whether Redwood's private deployment option will be required for these runs or if hosted Dedicated pools are sufficient?

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@globex.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: mixed real-world load benchmark + scaling behavior

Hi Priya — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Controlled failure scenarios and measurement:
   - Node drop: orchestrate draining + abrupt node termination; measure time to restore target QPS and 99th-latency after failover.
   - Inter-region latency spike: inject network delay (tc/netem) to one region and observe routing/fallback behavior; measure request loss, fallback time, and SLO gap.
   - KV cache cold-start: evict caches and measure token cost and latency until steady-state (we'll report warm-up curves).

   Measurement approach: synchronized timestamps, synthetic probe requests interleaved with real workload, and recovery-time defined as time until 95% of pre-failure QPS and 99th-latency baseline.

2) Quantization quality checks:
   - We'll provide a labeled prompt-set (200 prompts per model class) with reference completions and compute ROUGE/embedding-similarity deltas. Acceptance thresholds: <= 2% embedding cosine drop and <= 3 points ROUGE-L for GLUE-like tasks (customizable per customer).

3) Data artifacts for audit:
   - Yes, we can provide anonymized raw logs (request id, timestamp, latency, model_variant, node_id) and aggregated CSV metrics. We will redact PII and provide a data processing manifest.

Hosted vs Private: For initial benchmarking runs: Hosted Dedicated pools are sufficient and far faster to provision; Private (VPC/on-prem) can be used if you require traffic to remain inside your network. We'll note cost and lead-time differences in the run estimate.

Next steps: we will upload the runner harness, kernel CSV, and a short reproducibility README to the linked Drive by EOD tomorrow. Vanessa will share the run-time and cost forecast in a separate note. If Globex agrees, we can schedule a kick-off on Friday to align on seed prompts and the Poisson arrival parameters.

Thanks — look forward to running this.

Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
